column3: So why would a brain do this to itself?
Part of the answer is simple. It feels better. Not checking, doubting the bad news, seeing a slightly better face in the mirror. All of it protects how we feel about ourselves.

Some researchers go further. Psychologists William von Hippel and Robert Trivers have argued that self deception may have evolved because the most convincing way to persuade other people is to believe it yourself.
That's a theory, not a settled fact. But it fits with how often the lies we tell ourselves are the flattering ones.
And honestly? A little of this might even help us get out of bed in the morning.
The problem is when the thing you won't look at is the thing that matters most.
